title: Stashing Work & Release Tagging
description: Shelve unfinished changes temporarily with git stash and mark milestone releases with lightweight and annotated tags.

blocks.content:
## Shelving In-Progress Work with `git stash`

Frequently, an urgent bug fix demands switching branches while your current feature is half-written and not ready to commit. `git stash` takes your uncommitted modifications (both staged and unstaged) and saves them onto a dirty working directory stack, reverting your working tree to clean HEAD state.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    WT["Working Directory (Half-finished edits)"] -->|"git stash save"| Stack[("Git Stash Stack\nstash@{0}\nstash@{1}")]
    Stack -->|"git stash pop"| Restored["Working Directory (Cleaned then Restored)"]
```

## Common Stash Commands

```bash
# Stash modified tracked files with a descriptive label
git stash push -m "wip: shopping cart checkout flow"

# Stash including untracked new files
git stash -u

# List all saved stashes on the stack
git stash list
# Output: stash@{0}: On feature-cart: wip: shopping cart checkout flow

# Apply most recent stash AND remove it from the stack
git stash pop

# Apply stash but keep it on the stack for re-use
git stash apply stash@{0}

# Delete a specific stash from the stack
git stash drop stash@{0}

# Clear all stashes permanently
git stash clear
```

## Marking Milestones with `git tag`

Tags mark specific release points in repository history (e.g. `v1.0.0`, `v2.4.1`). While branches move forward as new commits arrive, tags remain fixed to a single commit forever.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C1["C1"] --> C2["C2 (v1.0.0)"] --> C3["C3"] --> C4["C4 (v1.1.0, main)"]
```

### Lightweight vs Annotated Tags

| Tag Type | Command | Stored Data |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lightweight** | `git tag v1.0.0` | Simple pointer file containing only a commit SHA. |
| **Annotated** | `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release 1.0.0 stable"` | Full Git object with tagger name, email, date, message, and optional GPG signature. |

> Best Practice: Always use annotated tags (`-a`) for public software releases.

## Sharing Tags with Remotes

By default, `git push` does not transfer tags to remote servers. You must push tags explicitly:

```bash
# Push a specific tag
git push origin v1.0.0

# Push all local tags at once
git push origin --tags

# Delete a remote tag
git push origin --delete v1.0.0
```

blocks.question: What is the key functional difference between a Git branch and a Git tag?
options: Branches can only be viewed in the terminal, while tags exist only on GitHub
Branches automatically advance when new commits are added, while tags remain fixed to a specific commit
Tags can be committed to, but branches cannot
Tags require a paid server license to create
blocks.explanation: Branches are moving pointers that advance as new commits arrive. Tags are permanent, static milestone markers pinned to one commit.

blocks.question: Which command restores stashed changes into your working directory and removes them from the stash list?
blocks.explanation: 'git stash pop' applies the top-most stash (stash@{0}) back onto the working tree and immediately removes it from the stash stack. 'git stash apply' applies without removing.
